title: Experimental Observation of Anomalous Complementary Weak Values from Correlated Pairwise Two-State Vectors
authors: Qian Xie, Liang Xu, Lijian Zhang
abstract: Weak values (WVs) arise from weak measurements performed within a time-symmetric formulation of quantum mechanics, where a system is both pre- and post-selected. Anomalous WVs that lie far outside the eigenvalue spectrum of the observable hold both fundamental and practical significance. However, their generation typically relies on near-orthogonal pre- and post-selection, which confines them to a single post-selection outcome with extremely low success probability. This constraint limits experimental accessibility and hinders the full exploitation of time symmetry. To overcome these limitations, we utilize quantum entanglement and post-selection-controlled operations to generate correlated pairwise two-state vectors. By changing the role of post-selection from passive filtering to active engineering, this approach enables the observation of anomalous complementary WVs associated with mutually exclusive post-selection branches. Our results extend the operational accessibility of time-symmetric quantum structures associated with the two-state vector formalism, and open new avenues for exploring the applications of time symmetry in quantum information processing.
summary: The paper presents an experimental method to observe anomalous complementary weak values that are otherwise inaccessible due to low success probabilities. By actively controlling post-selection using entangled photon pairs, the authors demonstrate a robust protocol that significantly enhances the measurement of time-symmetric quantum structures in photonic systems.
main_problem: The primary challenge is overcoming the low success probability associated with observing anomalous weak values (WVs) in standard time-symmetric quantum measurements.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated a post-selection-controlled protocol that enables the experimental observation of anomalous complementary WVs, significantly exceeding bounds set by standard measurement techniques.
method: They employ a technique utilizing quantum entanglement and controlled unitary operations to actively engineer correlated pairwise two-state vectors, allowing access to mutually exclusive post-selection branches.
model_or_system: The experiment is implemented on a photonic platform using two-photon polarization-entangled states generated via SPDC. The formalism relies on the Time-Symmetric Two-State Vector Formalism (TSVF).
key_observables: Anomalous complementary weak values ($f^\pm\langle\hat{O}angle_{w}^{i\pm}$), success probabilities, and Hong-Ou-Mandel interference visibility.
important_parameters: The anomalous WVs are analyzed in regimes yielding real or purely imaginary results based on relative phase tuning ($	heta_i - 	heta_f 	o \pi/2$ or $\phi_i - \phi_f 	o \pi$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the ability to implement controlled unitary operations and relies on comparing measured values against theoretical bounds derived from Cauchy-Schwarz inequalities.
figures_summary: Figures compare standard vs. post-selection-controlled protocols for real/imaginary WVs (Fig 3, S3) and show density matrix reconstruction fidelity and HOMI visibility (Fig S1).
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical limitation of standard WV measurements (Chunk 3), then details the proposed post-selection-controlled protocol using entanglement (Chunk 1 & 2), and finally compares the success probabilities and measured WVs between the two protocols, confirming operational accessibility (Chunk 4).
why_interesting: This work directly addresses fundamental limitations in measuring non-classical quantum effects like anomalous weak values by engineering measurement conditions, which is highly relevant to advanced quantum metrology and foundational quantum optics.

FIG. 2. Experimental Setup. (a) A continuous-wave laser at 405 nm pumps a periodically poled KTiOPO4 (PPKTP) crystal in the Sagnac interferometer, enabling spontaneous parametric down-conversion to prepare a two-photon polarization-entangled state. (b) Measurement of the WVs. (c) The post-selection-controlled structure, composed of ˆUf, a controlled-Z gate followed by a projective measurement on the ancilla. Abbreviations: DM, dichroic mirror; APD, avalanche photodiode; TDC, time-to- digital converter.

Figure 2 (b) illustrates the experimental setup for WV measurement. First, a polarizing beam displacer (PBD) maps the polarization-encoded QS to spatial modes: |H⟩→|0⟩(upper path) and |V ⟩→|1⟩(lower path). A HWP at 45◦in path 1 initializes both paths in the same polarization state |H⟩, which serves as the MS. The QS observable is taken to be ˆO = −ˆσz. The coupling Hamil- tonian ˆH = −gˆσz ⊗ˆσy is realized by rotating H1 (in path 1) to g/2 degrees and H2 (in path 0) to −g/2 degrees. Since the measurements on the MS (MMS) and post- selection of the QS act on separate Hilbert spaces, they commute and can be performed independently.
